subject: Post-discovery: technical runbook and latency evidence for HealthBridge pilot
messages:
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwood.com>
To: Elena Soto <elena@healthbridge.com>, Mike Carter <mike.carter@healthbridge.com>
Cc: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-10-07T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Post-discovery: technical runbook and initial model shortlist

Hi Elena / Mike —

Thanks again for taking the time this morning. Quick recap and clear next steps so momentum stays up: we validated the scope (real-time triage assistant for claims intake), discussed throughput targets (~120 QPS sustained during peak batch processing windows), and confirmed the main success criteria: answer accuracy on policy extraction >= 92% and end-to-end P95 latency under 220ms for the primary path.

What Im attaching / linking below:
- A short technical runbook draft (pilot_scope_v2.pdf) outlining the light-weight infra wed deploy for a 6-week proof-of-value: dedicated model route, KV-cache for session prompts, and autoscaling thresholds.
- Redwood-verified model profiles (redwood_verified_profiles.csv): candidate models with measured TPS, p50/p90/p99 latencies at the sequence lengths you described, and recommended quantization profiles.
- Raw latency traces (hb_latency_traces.zip) from our synthetic runs using your sample prompts (sanitized). These are the traces we used to compute the P95 numbers in the CSV.

Model shortlist (first-pass):
- rwinf-3b-q4: best cost / latency balance for short policy extraction prompts (p50 ~ 38ms, p95 ~ 140ms at 64-token windows)
- rwinf-7b-quant: higher accuracy for multi-turn context, expect ~8-12% quality lift on longer prompts but p95 increases (~210ms)
- optx-13b-serve: quality leader for ambiguous policy language; consider only for the fallback route where strict accuracy matters and latency tolerance is higher.

Known quality regression risk: for templates with unusually long policy excerpts (>400 tokens) we see hallucination spikes on smaller quantized models. We recommend a prompt-guard that routes those to the 7b or 13b variants and a short closed-set reranker to protect precision for named-entity outputs.

Next steps I propose (actionable):
1) Approve pilot scope and sign off on the test dataset we used (Ill drop the sanitized CSV into the Drive folder) — Elena to confirm by 10/12.
2) We spin up a 2-week evaluation run with three routes (3b baseline, 7b primary, 13b fallback) and collect latency + quality telemetry — Redwood to provision by 10/14 once scope is approved.
3) Joint guardrail review after week 1 to tune reranker thresholds — schedule 30m with your engineering lead.

If that plan looks good Ill send a calendar invite and a short pilot SOW.

Thanks —
Rafael

--
Rafael Mendes | Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
rafael@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0123

From: Elena Soto <elena@healthbridge.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwood.com>
Cc: Mike Carter <mike.carter@healthbridge.com>
Date: 2027-10-07T12:01:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-discovery: technical runbook and initial model shortlist

Thanks Rafael — helpful summary. A few clarifying notes from our side:

- The 120 QPS target is correct but its bursty (incoming claims arrive in 10–15 minute spikes). Can you confirm whether Redwoods autoscaling can handle 4x baseline for those windows without rewarming penalties?
- For accuracy: 92% on extraction is our target but were more sensitive to precision on claimant names and policy numbers — false positives there are high cost.

We looked quickly at the CSV and like the direction. Two asks:
1) Can you provide the prompt set you used to generate the traces (so we can run local verification)?
2) Can you mark which examples in the traces triggered hallucination on the 3b quant baseline so we can see patterns?

If you can get those over today / tomorrow well aim to greenlight the pilot by 10/12.

Elena

Elena Soto | Head of Automation | HealthBridge
elena@healthbridge.com | +1 (617) 555-0987

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwood.com>
To: Elena Soto <elena@healthbridge.com>, Mike Carter <mike.carter@healthbridge.com>
Cc: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-10-07T15:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-discovery: technical runbook and initial model shortlist

Elena — great questions. Quick answers and the two items you requested attached/linked: see prompt_set_v1.txt in the Drive folder and a small CSV (trace_annotations.csv) with the 28 trace segments where the 3b baseline produced low-confidence or hallucinated outputs. Highlights:

- Autoscaling: Redwoods Dedicated route uses warm pool policy by default; we configure a short rewarm window (60s) for GPU-backed routes. For your pattern we recommend an initial warm pool sized for ~1.5x baseline and a burst policy of ~3x that uses pre-warmed instances. In our synthetic spike tests the p95 did not exceed 260ms during 3.5x bursts when using the recommended warm pool. Well share the raw trace that shows the rewarm timeline.
- Prompt set: the prompt_set_v1 includes the exact templates we used (policy excerpt canonicalization + extraction markers) — you can run these locally.
- Hallucination markers: trace_annotations.csv tags the tokens/segments; the common cause we saw was ambiguous bullet formatting and truncated context.

Attachments / quick links:
- Pilot scope: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1a2b3c-pilot-scope-v2
- Prompt set: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1a2b3c-promptset-v1
- Verified profiles CSV: https://s3.redwood-inference.com/healthbridge/redwood_verified_profiles.csv
- Annotated traces: https://s3.redwood-inference.com/healthbridge/trace_annotations.csv

Well plan to provision the evaluation environment once you confirm the dataset. Camila / Aditya — can you reserve the Dedicated route and prewarm config mentioned above for 10/14? Priyom — please add a small reranker recipe to the shared notebook and Ill send a link.

Thanks, Rafael

--
Rafael Mendes | Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference

From: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.com>
To: Elena Soto <elena@healthbridge.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwood.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-10-08T17:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-discovery: technical runbook and initial model shortlist

Hi Elena — quick operational note from the infra side:

- Reserved: Ive provisioned a Dedicated route with the warm pool and burst policy Rafael recommended. Hostnames and access are in the Drive doc (pilot infra playbook).
- Validation checklist: well run three canonical traces (short, medium, long) and upload the telemetry to the shared S3 folder. Expect the first validation run by EOD 10/14.
- Reranker: Priyom has added a Jupyter cell with a simple closed-set rerank using cosine similarity over entity embeddings; its in the notebook at: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-redwood-healthbridge-eval (see notebook cell "simple_rerank_v1").

If you want any adjustments to the warm pool sizing before we run the smoke tests let us know today so we can tweak infra.

—Camila
